_readme: InoxTv AdMob (GMA) remote config — ONE file, both apps.
Host at: https://jitendrasoftwaredeveloper.github.io/inoxtv-config/inoxtv-admob.json
preroll.json is a DIFFERENT file and belongs to the IMA / VAST / VMAP live-TV path.
Nothing in this file touches it, reads it, or can affect an IMA ad.
SWITCHES, widest first — each one is a single edit, no app release:
1. master_enabled ............... false = no GMA ad anywhere, both apps, all build types
2. debug_ads_enabled ........... false = no GMA ad in DEBUG builds, both apps
3. <platform>.master_enabled ... false = that one app goes silent, the other keeps running
4. slots.<name>.enabled ........ false = that one placement goes silent
A slot key the app asks for but this file does not contain behaves exactly like enabled:false.
THIS FILE HOLDS EXACTLY WHAT THE APP ASKS FOR — 9 mobile keys, 1 TV key, nothing else.
The 9 mobile keys are the same 9 in MobileAdMobHost.slotFallbacks, one for one. Adding a key
the code does not read does NOTHING: it is parsed, stored and never looked up. So a new
placement is always code first, then a key here — never a key here in the hope it turns on.
WHAT THE CODE ACTUALLY READS. Everything else here is documentation for whoever edits the file:
top level ..... master_enabled, debug_ads_enabled, allow_test_units_in_release
per platform .. reward_gates, reward_unlock_hours, slots
per slot ...... enabled, live, test, min_interval_s (app_open only), max_per_session (int only)
NOT read ...... version, updated, publisher, app_id, name, format, phase, console_refresh_s,
_note, _readme
console_refresh_s is the value you set in the AdMob console, recorded here so this file tells
the whole story. The app cannot change a banner's refresh rate, so editing that number here
changes nothing — change it on the ad unit in the console.
Unknown keys are ignored and missing keys take their defaults, so this file can gain keys
later without breaking an app already installed in the field.
EVERY DEFAULT IS THE QUIET ONE. A missing or misspelled enabled reads as false, a missing
max_per_session reads as 0 = never, a missing master_enabled reads as false. A file that loses
a key goes silent, never loud. The one deliberate exception is reward_gates: an empty or
missing value means NO gate is active, because a broken config must never lock a user out of a
feature. Ads fail towards showing less; gates fail towards giving more.
allow_test_units_in_release: true = RELEASE builds serve Google DEMO ads instead of your real ones.
It reads slots.<name>.test directly, so live is never touched and there is nothing to revert but
this one boolean. Use it ONLY for the R8 / minified-APK check, then set it back to false.
Left true in production it earns exactly ZERO while every ad still displays perfectly. It is the
one key in this file whose wrong value costs money rather than just showing nothing.
An empty live is NOT a kill switch. It falls through to the ID compiled into the app as the
fetch-failure fallback. Those compiled fallbacks are all empty strings today, so an empty live
does show nothing right now — but the moment real IDs are compiled in, it would start serving.
To silence a placement for certain, always use enabled:false.
publisher and app_id here are DOCUMENTATION for whoever hand-edits this file. The resolver
validates every unit ID against a COMPILED-IN publisher prefix, never against the publisher
field in this same file — a document checked against itself is not checked. A live ID that
fails that prefix is ignored and the compiled fallback is used instead. Neither value is a
secret: both already ship in plain text inside every APK, and app-ads.txt publishes the
publisher on purpose. Never put anything that authenticates in here (AdMob API/OAuth, service
accounts, keys).
SLOT KEY vs name — two different naming systems, joined only by the ID:
the slot KEY (player_fullscreen_banner) is what the app's code reads. Renaming it is a code
change, so it never changes.
name (INX_MOB_BAN_PLAYER_FULLSCREEN) is only the label you typed into the AdMob console. NO
code reads it. Rename it in the console whenever you like — the app cannot tell. It sits here
so this file alone tells you which console unit's ID belongs in which live field.
format = what to pick at the console's 'Ad format' step. It is fixed when the unit is created:
a Native unit can never serve a banner, so a placement that changes format needs a NEW unit.
phase = rollout stage. Both are documentation, same as publisher/app_id.
_note = which screens the slot actually serves, so this file answers that without reading code.
TEST vs LIVE — keep BOTH, never overwrite one with the other:
test = Google's demo unit. Always fills, never touches your account, safe to click.
live = your real unit from the AdMob console. Paste it in; leave test where it is.
Overwriting test with live means a debug build can never show an ad again, and the next
4dp banner tweak would need a release build to verify.
CURRENT STATE (2026-08-26) = LIVE. Real IDs are in place on every slot.
debug_ads_enabled is true, so DEBUG builds serve Google demo ads and RELEASE builds serve the
real units. A debug build can never reach a live unit whatever this file says: the resolver
returns test whenever BuildConfig.DEBUG, before live is even looked at. Setting
debug_ads_enabled false therefore silences debug builds only, and does not touch release.
Every live field is filled, mobile and TV alike, so no slot here is waiting on console work.
playlist_processing_banner was the last to land.
ONE slot is deliberately off — section_switch_int. It is fully implemented; flipping enabled to
true starts showing it with no release.
REMOVED 2026-08-26 — four keys no code read were deleted from this file, because a config that
advertises placements the app cannot serve is a config that lies:
player_pause_native ......... INX_MOB_NAT_PLAYER_PAUSE ......... /1440492568
playlist_processing_native .. INX_MOB_NAT_PLAYLIST_PROCESSING .. /1360601519
catalog_grid_native ......... INX_MOB_NAT_CATALOG_GRID ......... /2784479346
vod_entry_rewint ............ INX_MOB_REWINT_VOD_ENTRY ......... /7239614153
Their IDs are recorded above only so the console units can be found and deleted. They were
dropped on purpose, not overlooked: a native ad inside a tap-to-play poster grid or on a pause
overlay collects mis-tap clicks, mis-taps are invalid traffic, and invalid traffic is enforced
at ACCOUNT level — it would risk the working banner and rewarded revenue to chase a third
format. vod_entry_rewint would charge a second ad for a journey the rewarded gate on movies and
shows already covers. Re-adding any of these keys does nothing until app code reads it.
TWO REWARDED UNITS, NOT ONE. mobile.slots.unlock_rew.live and tv.slots.unlock_rew.live are
different inventory under different AdMob apps. Pasting the same ID into both would
mis-attribute every impression in the account. The demo ID is legitimately the same string
in both — only the live IDs differ.
reward_gates: comma list from movies,shows,search,record,addplaylist,theme. Empty = no gate
is active even when unlock_rew is enabled, so every feature stays free.
reward_unlock_hours: clamped to 1-720 in code. 0, negative, or unparseable falls back to 6 —
an unclamped 0 would re-lock the feature the instant the ad finished.
mobile and tv hold this value INDEPENDENTLY. Today mobile is 6 and tv is 3, so a TV user
re-watches an ad twice as often as a phone user for the same feature. That is a real product
difference rather than a default — if it was not intended, set tv to 6 here.
New ad units return error code 3 (no fill) for a few hours up to ~24h after creation.
That is not a bug. Wait it out.

unlock_rew.name: INX_MOB_REW_UNLOCK
unlock_rew._note: The feature gates listed in reward_gates. Never a paywall: if this slot goes quiet the gate opens rather than locking the user out.

app_open.name: INX_MOB_APPOPEN_RESUME
app_open._note: Shown on a real return to the foreground only. Never on first launch, never on rotation, never on internal navigation, and never over a return the app itself asked for (external player, file picker, consent form, store).

fullscreen_exit_int.name: INX_MOB_INT_FULLSCREEN_EXIT
fullscreen_exit_int._note: Leaving a fullscreen player — live TV, movies, shows. The player exits first and the ad opens over the screen behind it, so the user is never held in fullscreen waiting on an ad. max_per_session 0 or missing means never.

section_switch_int.name: INX_MOB_INT_SECTION_SWITCH
section_switch_int._note: IMPLEMENTED but switched off. Flip enabled to true to start showing it, no release needed. Fires only on a real sidebar section change, never on re-selecting the section already open.

livetv_browse_banner.name: INX_MOB_BAN_LIVETV_BROWSE
livetv_browse_banner._note: Serves the live-TV browse band AND the live-TV fullscreen band. They are the same physical band, kept on one unit so toggling fullscreen does not throw away a loaded ad.

catalog_browse_banner.name: INX_MOB_BAN_CATALOG_BROWSE
catalog_browse_banner._note: Movies, Shows, Recordings and My List browse bands.

player_fullscreen_banner.name: INX_MOB_BAN_PLAYER_FULLSCREEN
player_fullscreen_banner._note: Movies and Shows fullscreen players only. Live-TV fullscreen is served by livetv_browse_banner instead — see its note.

onboarding_banner.name: INX_MOB_BAN_ONBOARDING
onboarding_banner._note: The whole playlist-setup flow — welcome home, the type picker, and the M3U, Xtream, Stalker and EPG form pages. Six screens on one unit on purpose: they are the lowest-volume placements in the app and the user sees exactly one at a time, so splitting them would divide the impressions that teach AdMob what this inventory is worth. The delete-confirm page carries no band and never will, because a banner beside a destructive button is a mis-tap trap.

playlist_processing_banner.name: INX_MOB_BAN_PLAYLIST_PROCESSING
playlist_processing_banner._note: The playlist-processing screen — the longest-dwell screen in the app, because importing a large M3U or Xtream playlist takes minutes. On its own unit rather than sharing onboarding_banner's because AdMob prices a unit on the behaviour it sees, and mixing a several-minute screen in with six screens the user passes through in seconds would teach it the wrong thing about both.

unlock_rew.name: INX_TV_REW_UNLOCK
unlock_rew._note: The ONLY ad the TV app serves, by design. TV has no banner, no app-open and no interstitial: the TV host returns null for attachBanner and calls onDone straight through for interstitials, so a banner or interstitial slot added to this section would be parsed and then ignored.
